newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Further talks to avert S.African trucking strike.
newsitem.headline: Further talks to avert S.African trucking strike.

text.p: The Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA), set up in terms of South Africa's new Labour Relations Act, has intervened in a bid to avert Wednesday's planned trucking industry strike.

Transport and General Workers' Union (TGWU) national organiser Thulani Dlamini told Reuters CCMA convenors had proposed to mediate in the deadlocked wage talks should the union agree to another meeting with employers.
"We were approached by the CCMA and have agreed to another meeting at 1400 GMT today (Tuesday) between ourselves and employers to be steered by CCMA co-ordinator Charles Nupen," Dlamini said.

The meeting is a last-ditch attempt to avert a strike by around 36,000 workers which would affect major sectors of the economy including banking, air freight, waste companies, livestock vehicles, and the ferrying of chemicals and fuels.
Trucker blockades on major highways are also a possibility if employers do not confiscate trucks from workers.

Employers and the seven unions organised in the sector are deadlocked over wages and working conditions, with union's last revised wage demand at 12.5 percent across-the-board from an original 14 to 18 percent across-the-board increase.
Employers, represented by the Road Freight Association, have upped their offer to 10 percent across-the-board from an original nine percent.
Wage talks deadlocked in late September after employers offered a then final nine percent.
Dlamini said earlier this week the strike committee had approached other Congress of South African Trade Union affiliates and would know by Thursday if truckers could expect secondary support action.
If the strike cannot be averted, it will be the first time in 50 years that workers in the sector resort to industrial action.
Employer representatives were not immediately available to comment.
The South African Police Service (SAPS) on Tuesday voiced its concern at the threatened strike action and called upon unions to act within the bounds of the law should they resort to strike action.
It said was particularily concerned about public and private road blockades.

Seven unions are organised in the trucking industry, including the TGWU, the Professional Transport Workers' Union, African Miners and Allied Workers, the Turning Wheel Workers' Union, the Motor Transport Workers' Union, the South African Transport Workers' Union and the Transport and Allied Workers' Union.
The average wage in the industry is 321 rand per week for general workers in the bigger centres.
